runs.note: Reproduces run 2's observations with the reviewed fixture (comma-count tags, ER-010 collapse warnings, store reset on restart); single-run fixture figures, not a performance comparison

observations: x-request-id is preserved end to end from these LAN clients (observed). When it is absent the Gateway adds one, plus x-forwarded-for, x-forwarded-proto and x-envoy-internal; x-envoy-internal was seen only on that raw probe without x-request-id. A likely explanation for preservation is that Envoy classes LAN clients as internal and so does not regenerate the header, but that was not observed directly.

Repeated x-vuoro-identity arrives as two separate headers; repeated x-request-id arrives joined into one comma-separated value. Both shapes are refused (identity) with no owner effect on all four arms.
HTTP and Connect routes reach the backend as HTTP/1.1 even when the client negotiates HTTP/2; only the gRPC route (Service appProtocol h2c) reaches it as HTTP/2.

The Gateway translates grpc-web (HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2) on the gRPC hostname into native gRPC; a signed grpc-web publication reached the fixture and changed owner state (status 200; grpc-status was not surfaced in response headers).

Raw HTTP/1.1 header names keep case-insensitive matching, padding is trimmed, comma values are kept, duplicates stay separate, and header names containing underscores (x_ec00_underscore) are forwarded unchanged. The production verifier (FastAPI/ASGI, gateway_identity.py) matches exact header names and no underscore identity header was sent, so this is not an observed bypass; rejecting or dropping underscore header names at the ingress or backend is a candidate defence-in-depth requirement, relevant to any backend that maps '_' to '-' (WSGI/CGI).

Latency (client wall time, reused connection, n=20, first request excluded): HTTP v2 signed publication p50 9.28 / p95 14.53 ms; gRPC 11.45 / 14.46 ms; Connect JSON 55.81 / 59.97 ms; Connect binary 55.66 / 60.26 ms. Connect has a ~41 ms floor already present over local loopback (uvicorn/HTTP/1.1 path); over the Gateway, signed Connect adds about 14 ms against about 8-10 ms for HTTP v2 and gRPC. Only the floor is not attributed to the Gateway. No cross-candidate performance claim is made from this sample.
